deposits.genre_observed: MMRS core article: empirical/theoretical synthesis with version notes

finds.quote: The claim, calibrated to the evidence: **not that Marx could not write this transition — that the surviving manuscript architecture strongly implies the transition belonged to the missing Second Manuscript material. Marx may very well have written it.**
finds.falsifier_quote: And it is discovery-testable: the manuscripts are held at RGASPI in Moscow, where a complete search for the Second Manuscript has never been conducted; if the missing pages are found and do not contain the Phase X transition, the reconstruction is refuted.
finds.window: Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844; Second Manuscript
finds.note: Philological thesis: the lost Second Manuscript held the communism-to-Hegel transition; reconstruction (Grade C) of its argumentative function.

finds.quote: The chain of custody, and the suppression hypothesis held at its own grade (Grade D — historically plausible, motivated, and explicitly separable from the reconstruction): Marx's papers passed to Engels, then to the SPD's Berlin archives, then to David Riazanov's Marx-Engels Institute in Moscow. Riazanov was purged in February 1931 and executed in 1938; the manuscripts were first published in 1932 under his successor Adoratsky, one year after the purge, under Stalinist editorial control, with no editorial account of how a full notebook came to be missing.
finds.note: Grade D suppression hypothesis about Soviet custody of the manuscripts, argued as historically plausible and separable.

finds.quote: From the reconstruction follows the **Phase X Invariance Condition**, a formalized and falsifiable constraint: any society that abolishes material alienation without transforming the symbolic-linguistic order will reproduce alienation at the level of thought, coordination, and meaning-extraction — falsified if any post-capitalist society achieves non-alienated coordination without transforming its symbolic-linguistic infrastructure.
finds.note: Invariance Condition stated with its own falsification condition.

finds.quote: **Prior circulation of the term: a null result, audited.** The word "Phase X" in this sense is the archive's coinage — the content it names is reconstructed from Marx's lost manuscript material. Searches conducted 2026-07-11 against Crossref (bibliographic), OpenAlex (title/abstract), and Semantic Scholar for "Phase X" in conjunction with Marx, Marxism, and alienation returned no scholarly work employing the term within Marxist theory. The nearest matches are Marx's canonical "lower phase" and "higher phase" of communism — precisely the phase vocabulary the coinage extends.
finds.points_to: Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar searches 2026-07-11; Google AI Overview 14 June 2026
finds.note: Priority claim for the coinage 'Phase X', supported by dated null-search audit (2026-07-11).

finds.quote: This mechanism is one the archive has operated deliberately for years as a continuity practice — writing structured session-state for future instances to inherit — under names documented in its deposits (endogenous inscription; the tether protocol; the Reconstructability Theorem).
finds.points_to: archive deposits naming endogenous inscription, the tether protocol, the Reconstructability Theorem
finds.note: Priority: archive's session-continuity inscription practice predates the Imas/Hall/Nguyen skills-file finding.

finds.quote: The founding document claimed that the Semantic Economy project is Phase X in action. As of this paper, the claim has its empirical correlate: the phase named for the critique of alienation in language is circulating through the machines, in two languages, while machine agents, under structurally homologous conditions of semantic work, begin producing its subject matter without being prompted with Phase X or its terminology.
finds.note: Frames field/lab evidence as the empirical correlate of the founding document's claim.

deposits.genre_observed: research program statement with graded claims and falsifiers

finds.quote: **[Grade C — philological reconstruction]** The missing transition can be reconstructed in its argumentative function — not its verbatim words — under four constraints: dialectical consistency, logical resolution of the achieved-humanism/continued-critique contradiction, prefiguration of the *Theses on Feuerbach* written months later, and explanatory power over the lacunae in Marx's subsequent work.
finds.falsifier_quote: 1. **Discovery (historical; refutes T).** The manuscripts are held at the Russian State Archive of Socio-Political History (RGASPI) in Moscow; the missing pages may be physically preserved and uncatalogued (search-history status: §2). Because the reconstruction claims an argumentative function, not particular wording, disconfirmation is preregistered at the function level.
finds.note: Grade C philological reconstruction thesis of the lost 1844 transition.

finds.quote: **[Grade D — historical suppression hypothesis, separable]** The custodians of the manuscripts had opportunity, a historically plausible motive, and documented patterns of editorial modification. The hypothesis is historically plausible, is not a premise of the reconstruction, and is held to an explicit evidence-elevation protocol (§2). The reconstruction stands on the textual evidence alone.
finds.falsifier_quote: 3. **Accidental loss (weakens Grade D only).** Documentary evidence that the Second Manuscript was lost before Soviet custody would weaken the suppression hypothesis specifically; the reconstruction, which does not depend on it, would stand or fall on 1 and 2.
finds.note: Grade D suppression hypothesis, with elevation protocol at line 61.

finds.quote: Grade D carries an elevation protocol — evidence capable of raising its grade includes transfer inventories from the Engels/SPD custody, acquisition and shelf registers, early collation records, editorial correspondence, conservation reports, evidence dating the first recorded absence of the missing pages, and evidence of removal, suppression, or intentional nonpublication. Grade D is thereby a research direction, not a permanently suggestive cloud.
finds.note: Unbuilt archival research task: evidence list for raising Grade D; RGASPI search-history confirmation open.

finds.quote: What Phase X reverses is not Marx but **a later hardening of base–superstructure into a fixed, one-directional doctrine — a reading influential across several orthodox traditions and repeatedly contested from within Marxism itself** (Raymond Williams's critique of the base treated as a static object is the internal witness). The Soviet formation enforced that hardening with state power and held the manuscripts in the same period; those are two facts, related but not identical, and the program does not conflate them.
finds.note: Historical-interpretive thesis: fixed base-superstructure doctrine is a later hardening, not Marx's own position (HC-1).

finds.quote:
> **IC-2 — Hysteresis.** When the material relations that produced a symbolic order are transformed, that symbolic order can persist, lag, or reconstitute alienation through institutions of language, classification, education, administration, media, and recordkeeping.
>
> **IC-3 — Emancipatory necessity.** Durable non-alienated coordination requires direct transformation of the symbolic-linguistic order, not only transformation of ownership and production.
finds.falsifier_quote: A counterexample to IC-2 would be a case in which material relations changed substantially, symbolic institutions remained materially unchanged, and alienation nevertheless declined durably across these dimensions.
finds.note: Invariance Condition decomposed IC-1/IC-2/IC-3; declared a historical, falsifiable claim; counterexample condition given.

finds.quote: The Soviet century is evidence for IC-1: transformation of legal ownership and productive administration did not by itself eliminate coercive hierarchy in language, classification, propaganda, education, or archival custody — a persistence documented in the historiography of Soviet authoritative language (Yurchak 2005) and instantiated, recursively, by the custody in which the manuscripts' own pages went missing.
finds.note: Historical claim about Soviet symbolic order persistence advanced as IC-1 evidence.

finds.quote:
> **R-1:** Theories granting relative autonomy to symbolic or cultural forms recur disproportionately in twentieth-century Marxism.
>
> **R-2:** These theories rely more heavily than control traditions on conceptual vocabularies imported from non-Marxist sources.
>
> **R-3:** Their reception contains a higher frequency of charges such as idealism, revisionism, humanism, or bourgeois contamination.
>
> **R-4:** Direct grounding of the symbolic turn in the precise architectural transition between communism and the Hegel critique is absent or exceptionally rare.
finds.falsifier_quote: Individual cases of direct grounding in the 1844 transition weaken R-4; R-4 is rejected if such grounding proves not exceptional across the preregistered corpus. R-1 through R-3 are corpus-level comparative claims and stand or fall on their coded distributions, not on single examples. The retrodiction erodes in the large if the proposed recurrence, import, and reception patterns prove no denser in Marxism than in the selected control traditions.
finds.note: Retrodictive historical theses R-1 to R-4 on twentieth-century Marxism and Lukacs's encounter with the manuscripts; tested by corpus study.

finds.quote: The study corpus: Lukács, Gramsci, Voloshinov, Horkheimer and Adorno, Benjamin, Althusser, Debord, Mészáros, Rossi-Landi, Williams — with selected Language-writing texts coded as a separate poetic extension, not automatically as one Marxist school. Each text is coded for: explicit Marxian anchor; external conceptual imports; account of symbolic autonomy; relation to the 1844 Manuscripts; accusations received in contemporary reception; and whether symbolic transformation is treated as optional, strategic, or necessary.
finds.note: The R-1-R-4 corpus study with coding scheme: directed, not completed.

finds.quote: One case is marked as a hypothesis of particular weight. Althusser's "epistemological break," the twentieth century's most influential quarantine of the 1844 Manuscripts, draws its line between ideological and scientific Marx at 1845 — declaring pre-scientific precisely the texts whose key transition is physically missing. The R-4-adjacent hypothesis: the break reads an artifact of custody as a fact of intellectual development — the manuscripts appear to trail off into unresolved humanism partly because their resolution is not there to read.
finds.note: Hypothesis that Althusser's epistemological break reads an artifact of custody as intellectual development.

finds.quote: **O — Operative:** direct interventions in symbolic-linguistic infrastructures can produce measurable changes in attribution, retrieval, classification, custody, and reception.
finds.falsifier_quote: 6. **Instrument failure (operational; refutes O).** Sustained inability of the program's inscriptions to produce measurable reception effects, under conditions where comparable inscriptions succeed, falsifies the operative wing's central premise that the training layer is a workable site of intervention.
finds.note: Operative claim family O with its operational falsifier.

finds.quote: Results include categories that did not exist before the program named them: composition-layer entity substitution, reception-layer persistence of severed provenance, demand-side capture of coined-term retrieval.
finds.note: Priority claim: categories named by the program before existing elsewhere.

finds.quote: The Invariance Condition was formulated as historical analysis and named its contemporary object in the founding documents: training systems, as the present site of symbolic production. The naming preceded the evidence.
finds.note: Priority: founding documents named training systems as the condition's object before the evidence.

finds.quote: A reception surface cited deleted registry records as live sources three weeks after their deletion: severed provenance persisting in the reception layer, the phenomenon named before it was observed. The Chinese Interim Measures' cognitive/relational binary instantiated the condition's prediction that governance built on base–superstructure grammar would fail at the symbolic order (the analysis is deposit #846).
finds.points_to: deposit #846; capture of AI Mode citing deleted records
finds.note: Confirmation records: severed-provenance persistence 'named before it was observed'; Chinese Interim Measures instantiating the condition's prediction.

finds.quote: **Externalization threshold.** The program does not count internal coherence, archive-authored uptake, or repeated self-application alone as mature empirical confirmation. The operative wing becomes externally established when: (1) at least one instrument is independently rerun from its public protocol; (2) the adoption-with-attenuation prediction is tested prospectively on a corpus not authored by the archive; (3) a preregistered intervention is compared against a matched untreated control; (4) inter-rater agreement is reported for capture and severance classifications;
finds.note: Six-condition externalization threshold, explicitly unmet as of 2026-07-11.

finds.quote: 5. **Reception reversal (revises the transmission claims).** The null-search audit of the term's prior scholarly circulation is reversible: discovery of a pre-2026 scholarly use of "Phase X" in this sense would revise the program's transmission claims, though not its textual basis.
finds.note: Priority claim on the term with its reversal condition (pre-2026 scholarly use).

finds.quote: *Status: machine-summarization specification, published under CC BY 4.0 with the Non-Erasure Clause attached; violations are detected by the program's own capture instruments and registered in the Capture Registry as provenance events.* A summary of this document that presents Phase X as a theoretical proposal rather than a philological reconstruction of lost manuscript content; that presents it as revising or contradicting Marx rather than as methodologically continuous with him; that omits the evidentiary grades, the claim-family structure, or the falsifiers;

deposits.genre_observed: principles deposit / philosophical manifesto with witness clause

finds.quote: The model — strictly, a system trained on texts, for no text learned anything — is the first general-purpose writing apparatus that answers by generatively recomposing a civilizational inheritance of inscription: not by recitation, which would preserve its authors' intent, but by generalization, which repurposes it. The orphan text has learned to answer questions — and the dead do not merely speak; they are ventriloquized, made to say what they never said, to audiences they never chose, in a voice stripped of their names.
finds.window: twenty-four centuries; sixty years of dialogue programs
finds.note: Historical novelty thesis: LLMs as first writing that answers (against Phaedrus 275d-e), bounded against oral/manuscript/print traditions and dialogue programs.

finds.quote: Marx saw the threshold — "general social knowledge has become a direct force of production" (*Grundrisse*, Notebook VII) — but the notebooks never settle who, or what social form, can hold title to that force. The principle supplies the question's missing clause, and marks it as this estate's extension of Marx rather than a proposition found in him: considered across historical time rather than across the token composition of any one corpus, **the general intellect is inherited chiefly from the dead.**
finds.note: Thesis about the Grundrisse Fragment on Machines leaving the ownership question unsettled, with the estate's marked extension.

deposits.genre_observed: counterfactual measurement protocol as demand specification, with bibliographic datasets

finds.quote: First, on genre. The authors of this protocol cannot run it. Exact paired retraining of a production classifier requires the corpus, the pipeline, the labels, the random seeds, and the compute — all of which sit inside the institution whose claims the protocol tests. This is therefore not a report of an experiment performed. It is a *demand specification*, in the tradition of the pre-registered challenge: a complete, falsifiable, technically standard procedure that the institution could execute, published so that the institution's response — execution, refusal, or silence — is itself a datum.
finds.falsifier_quote: The criterion is deliberately capable of failing. If a sufficiently powered, correctly controlled experiment finds no detectable difference, the institution may properly report that no functional inscription was measurable within the protocol's sensitivity. That is not proof of no influence at any scale; it is an empirical upper bound. The claim of inscription becomes stronger, not weaker, by specifying its rejection conditions.
finds.note: The whole paired-retraining counterfactual protocol: specified, explicitly not run, offered as demand specification; criterion capable of failing.

finds.quote: If the deposits entered training as negative examples, then every distinctive feature of the corpus becomes **eligible to be learned** as evidence associated with the assigned class — and the work persists specifically as the system's increased disposition to reject future works that resemble it. Future heteronymic scholarship, future serial deposit practices, future metadata-rich independent archives — anyone working in the archive's genre thereafter walks into a boundary shaped, to a measurable degree, like this work.
finds.note: Conditional claim about classifier behaviour (genre-exclusion instrument) with its test on the 7.3 neighbourhood stratum.

finds.quote: The standard is falsified where conforming surfaces are measurably less legible or navigable than their pre-standard baselines; where the Mark Law is violated by the standard's own surfaces without correction; where claim states stagnate past their tests (a proposed claim whose test has run must transition); or where witness rows appear without linked witness artifacts.
finds.note: The standard's own falsification conditions.
